utterances.text: Could you tell Mr. Vanderpuye who was the immediate superior to General Galic in the hierarchy of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you see any evidence during your time in Sarajevo that General Galic received orders from anyone other than his immediate superior, General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALY ABDEL-RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened when I was reviewing the documents. I found a document and it surprised me. It contained orders from Dr. Koljevic whereby he issues order to co-operate with the civilians. I think that this was not normal. I know that the Serbian troops were very professional. We have had long-term relationship with them. They are very professional, and I don't think that this was the normal chain of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from this exception, do you have any evidence of other incidents where you -- that General Galic received orders from anyone else than his immediate superior? So apart from this Koljevic exception.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, sir. This was the only exception that I found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Judge Fluegge has one question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I would like to clarify one matter, and for that I need P302 on the screen, please. We don't have it yet.

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALY ABDEL-RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] I have it. I have it, sir, but I want to have it in focus, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have seen it earlier. Mr. Petrusic, in one of his questions, and this is on page 30 of today's transcript, was suggesting to you the following, and I quote: "Would you agree with me that General Galic issued this order on the basis of the order of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska as is stated at the end of this document that we have here?" I think there is a reference to an order by the Main Staff but not at the end but at the beginning of this. You see here on the screen the first line, "Pursuant to an order by the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska." I take it that this document is from the 10th of October, 1992. Before I put a question to you, I would now like to have D65, which is marked for identification, on the screen. We saw that earlier today too. This is a document signed by Mr. Mladic, dated 11th of November, 1992. Sir, can you help me? Could this order of the Commander Mladic of the 11th of November be the basis for the order we have seen dated 10th of October, 1992, which was suggested by Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALY ABDEL-RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The order of Mr. Mladic is dated 11th of November. The order by General Galic was dated 10th of October, much earlier than the order of Mr. Mladic, one month earlier.

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALY ABDEL-RAZEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, the main document that was issued pertaining to a cease-fire was another document, a different document, and I think it comprised something also pertaining to the Croatian troops, that they should be exempt from this order because they did not sign the agreement. Maybe this is an attachment to the main document whereby the orders of Mr. Galic were issued. However, should Galic issue any order, he should have received instructions from the higher command, and this is very normal in military hierarchy. When we have main instructions, they should be issued by the Supreme Command to the middle command, then to the staff underground or Executive Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I very well understand your general explanation. Thank you for that. That concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have the questions by the Bench triggered any need -- or if not. Mr. Abdel-Razek, I apologise for being three minutes late as far as the time you indicated you would like to be able to leave this courtroom. I would like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home and good health, and you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. Could the Defence meanwhile look into ID330, ID327, and ID335, which, if I'm not mistaken, are not yet tendered, whereas I think you announced, Mr. Petrusic, that you intended to tender them. 1D -- its -- yes, I say ID but I should say 1D for all three. Then after the break, is the witness ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There are a few special matters to be discussed before we start with the next witness. We'll deal with them at the beginning of the next session. We will resume -- take a break and resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could you please stand for a second. And I'd like to invite you to make a solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Witness RM081. Witness, you'll first be examined by Ms. D'Ascoli, and you'll find her to your right. Ms. D'Ascoli, are you ready to start your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli is counsel for the Prosecution as you may be aware of already. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Before I call up the pseudonym sheet I just wanted to advise the parties that we are proceeding in this way like we did previously with another protected witness, RM032, meaning that we have created a pseudonym sheet that also contains the name of certain person that might identify the witness, and in this way if the witness at any point feels that he needs to refer to these persons, he could refer to the names rather than -- sorry, to the numbers rather than the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you have instructed the witness thoroughly on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honours. And I would also ask later for leave to give one of these heard copies to the witness so he has it before himself and to the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, leave is granted already. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, I will now show you a document which contains personal information related to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I please have 65 ter 28443, not for public broadcast, of course. This is the pseudonym sheet of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, once the document is on the screen, I would ask you to have a look at it but not to read out loud the information contained in it, and I would ask you to confirm that what you see now on the screen, your name and your date of birth are correct. Please again do not repeat the information, just confirm whether this information related to your name and date of birth are correct.

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, sir, just a reminder of what we discussed during preparation for the testimony, you see a list of other names at the bottom part of this -- of this sheet. Just to remind you that because we are in public session, so if you need to refer to any of these individuals, please refer to them by the numbers that you see on the side. And I will now ask the Court Usher if they can give you a hard copy of this document so you have it with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have hard copies for Chambers, too, for the Judges, too. And I would now ask to -- I would now tender the pseudonym sheet mark with -- marked with 65 ter number 28433 [sic] into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28443 becomes Exhibit P308, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number you may have misspoken, Ms. D'Ascoli, or it may have been wrongly transcribed. It's 28443, which is the -- line 13 of this page you see that the number is different, but it's the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, it's 28443, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. P308 is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I now ask the Court Officer to call up 65 ter 28442, and again not for public broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Witness, while the document is brought up on the screen, do you remember providing a statement to the ICTY on 17 September 2011?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And now that the document is on the screen, can you please have a look at the signature at the bottom of the page in the original version of -- in the B/C/S document, and can you please tell us whether you recognise that signature.

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to read and review this statement in preparation for your appearance before the Court today?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, sir, are you satisfied that this is -- the statement is an accurate record of your evidence of what happened and what you experienced, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And if we -- if you -- if you were asked today the same questions that were asked in preparation for this statement, would you give the same answers in substance?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm that you provided that information in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 28442 pursuant to Rule 92 ter under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28442 becomes Exhibit P309 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P309 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, for ease of reference of the parties, we have also prepared a table of references of correspondence that shows the 65 ter numbers correspond -- the Mladic 65 ter numbers corresponding to the Karadzic ones that are used in the document so I would tender that document, too, at this stage. It is 65 ter 28373.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28373 becomes Exhibit P310, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. It needs to be under seal or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No it don't, Your Honours, also because when later we will tender public versions that will be useful to have it as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. There are also six associated exhibit to the witness statement now in evidence as P309. Upon review, we will only tender three today of these associated exhibit, so I'm going to tender one of these now together with the statement, and this is 65 ter 08895, and I would ask it to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 08895 becomes Exhibit P311 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P311 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I will then discuss and tender with the witness in direct examination 65 ter 08500 and 65 ter 09097. While with regard to 65 ter 09077 to which the Defence has objected in their response to RM081's 92 motion, at this stage we simply note that this witness, RM081, discusses this document in paragraph 98 of his statements, provide his comments, and we will tender this document from the bar table or through another witness at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And with the Chamber's leave I would like to read a summary of the witness's evidence for the public and the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have explained to the witness the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So a summary will now be read. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: The witness is a Bosnian Muslim from the municipality of Rogatica. He testifies about the takeover of Rogatica by Serb forces on 21/22 May 1992. The witness testifies that following the attack, announcement were made that Muslims without weapons should surrender themselves to the Serb authorities at the Vlahovic Secondary School. The witness went to the school with approximately 200 to 300 other Muslims. The school eventually held 1.100 people. Rajko Kusic was for a time the commander of the detection facility at the Vlahovic Secondary School. The witness was detained in the school for approximately three months and a half. He describes the deplorable living conditions at the school where detainees had insufficient food and water, opportunities to preserve personal hygiene were inadequate and sleeping quarters were overcrowded. The witness further testifies about beating, killings, and rapes at the school performed on detainees by the school guards. And that concludes the summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, it's only now that the translation finishes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you read, please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Witness RM081, I will now have a few questions for you today.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I please have on the screen 65 ter 09097. Public display is fine for this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Witness, I will show you a document that pertains to the events in Rogatica in May/June 1992. This document, Witness, is discussed in your statement. This is paragraph 39, for the record. And I would like to ask you to comment a bit more about it in addition to what is in your statement. This is an operative report from the Rogatica Brigade command dated the 11th of June, 1992, and addressed to the SRK command. Sir, first of all, can you have a look at the bottom of page 1 in the original document, and I -- I will ask you whether you recognise the name of the author of this order, of the commander who issued the order.

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the name, although it's not his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: The document is sent -- the author of the document is Commander Rajko Kusic, and you described Kusic's role in detailing your statement, so I won't ask further questions about that. I want to show you -- I want you to comment on the first sentence of the very first paragraph of the document. So maybe if we can zoom on the first paragraph of the B/C/S, please. Yes, the very top of the page. Sir, can you look at this very first sentence that says: "In the brigade's zone of responsibility, there were no sizable enemy activities." You can, of course, also read it for yourself in the original of the document. I want to ask you if this is consistent with what you observed in Rogatica in May and June 1992, and by that I mean whether according to your recollection, were there any significant enemy activities as it is said in this document, and considering the context of this document, enemy activities by non-Serb forces in the area of Rogatica? Is that consistent with your recollection of the events in that period?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: In essence, it is roughly the way it is stated in the first sentence of this document, but even if there was any activity in the area of Rogatica, I cannot say anything about that because I was in the very centre of town itself with a lot of other people, and in the town itself, there weren't any activities of ours because there were about 3.500 to 4.000 civilians, women, children, the elderly, and there were men of my age who were civilians and who had not had any contact with weapons. Quite simply, they happened to be where they were, and from that point of view this first sentence does make sense in terms of the overall situation in the town of Rogatica. However, as far as the centre of town is concerned --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. And just to clarify, when you say "there weren't any activities of ours," what do you mean by "ours"? Do you mean civilians? Do you mean Muslims? Do you mean your community? Can you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: What I thought of and as I tried to explain to you, these were men, people, civilians, lots of women, lots of children, lots of elderly people, lots of sick people. We had no possibility of carrying out any kind of activity. We stayed in Rogatica hoping that there wouldn't be any difficult situations there. While specifically for me personally ...

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Next, can you please have a look at the second sentence, and this says -- it's again the first paragraph, just the second sentence where it says: "Large numbers of Muslim civilians arrive in town every day, mostly women and children and unarmed people." And again can you tell us whether this corresponds to your experience of the events.

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Absolutely not, because at that time no one could enter Rogatica or leave Rogatica. What it says here, that the population was being put up at the secondary school, that was not the case. The population was being taken prisoner and then escorted by the Serb army brought to the secondary school where we were taken over by these guards, whatever they're called, people who were in charge of that. When people arrived in camp, they tried to be put up any way that was possible, and then two girls came and registered the persons who had been brought to the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Let me -- let me interrupt you there, Witness. You were, in fact, covering that -- I'm -- meaning like I was going to ask you a question about this other sentence that you just commented upon in the document. This is the third part of the third sentence of, again, the first paragraph where the document says: "The people are finding shelter or are being accommodated," depending on the translation, "in the secondary school centre?" And my question to you, I was going to ask you whether also this corresponded to your recollection to what actually was happening at the school for what you have seen it, but I take it from your answer that this is not correct; right?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Absolutely not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. And you described why not in your previous answer. So I will leave it there. My last question about this document is with regard to the first sentence of the second paragraph of the document. You can read it where it says: "Snipers are firing from one or two places in town." And my question is whether you remember snipers firing in town, Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: I said at the very beginning that in Rogatica, in the area where I moved about and where I happened to be as this situation occurred, there weren't any weapons there. There weren't any sniper shooters there. There weren't any military actions being taken by this civilian population. I did see sniper shooters. I did see that, but they belonged to the Serb army. You could see that with the naked eye, because the distance was from 50 to 100 to 150 to 200 metres roughly. I could see that. Other people could see that too. And Serb soldiers also had these nests from which they controlled the part of town where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is one of the associated exhibit, and I would tender it at this stage as a public exhibit, 65 ter 09097.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I have to object based upon the witness's testimony at transcript page 58, line 24, that this is not -- he recognises the signature is not belonging to the person that is the purported author; whereas in the statement it says that it is signed by this person Kusic, and the witness has just testified that this is not his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist me in taking us to the relevant paragraph of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 39, Your Honour, of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And today's transcript temporary page 58, line 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I clarify that with the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, could you please look again at the bottom of this first page where the -- the stamp of the -- the stamp and the signature of the author of this document, Commander Rajko Kusic, is. You said that -- so you of course recognise the -- this person, but you think that is not his signature; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: What is added in pencil is not his signature. At least it's not the signature that I know. And I think that I do know it well. And also it says here "za" for the commander. So somebody signed for the commander on behalf of the commander. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: That was my point. If we can have a look at the English version because normally these types of documents would be signed on behalf. So I just wanted to see if we have the same translation in the English. Page 2. Go to page 2. And it says "and written for," well, the signature for the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the only thing still to be clarified is in your statement, Witness, you said this is a document signed by Mr. Kusic. Do I understand that looking closer at it that you say the signature is, first of all, because I know his signature, this is not his signature, and that that was a mistake when you earlier said that it was signed by Mr. Kusic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Do the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That takes care of my objection, Your Honour. I withdraw the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 09097 becomes Exhibit P312, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P312 is admitted into evidence as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I now please have on the screen 65 ter 08500. And also public display is fine for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Witness, I will show you another document that you have already seen and discussed in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And for the record, this is at paragraph 55 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And again I would like to ask you a couple of more questions about it. This is a statement sheet for the security services centre, the police station of Rogatica, and lists the name of active policemen working in Rogatica in May 1992. Sir, can you see the document on the screen? Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: You're familiar with it; right?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, you have enumerated in your statement the people that you knew on this list and many of these individuals are also referred to in different parts of your statement. Now, just generally without going into name by name because we have the references to the names that you have recognised in the statement, can you tell us how you knew these people?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Well, I know all of these people because, first of all, Rogatica is not a big town. Well, I specifically knew all of these people because of the work that I did and then also on a personal level. So I can just say that I knew them very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And do you know if they were working at the Rogatica police station?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And from your statement, I take it that you saw some of these people at the Vlahovic Secondary School during the months in which you were detained there. For example, if we have a look -- if you have a look at the names listed in numbers 3, 11, and 19 of page 1, and I repeat, 3, 11, and 19, are these the names of the soldiers who were seen taking women out of the camp school to rape them? You should look at the document on the screen, not at the one on your table. And I will -- I just wanted to confirm with you that the names listed in the document on the screen at numbers 3, 11, and 19 are the names of the soldiers who were seen taking women out of the camp school to rape them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And now if you look at the name listed in number 37 on page 2, number 37, this person was questioning people, including you, at the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is also one of the associated exhibit, and I would tender it into evidence as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 08500 becomes Exhibit P313, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P313 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Witness, I now have a question about Rajko Kusic's presence at Vlahovic school. In your statement, you discuss a long visit by Kusic at the school, a visit that lasted about an hour during which Kusic said that people detained at the school and in Rogatica were not co-operating enough, that this was creating problems for him as he had a deadline for cleansing Rogatica and that he had to report to Pale about that. For the record, this is paragraph 90 of the witness statement. Sir, my question is quite a simple one: Do you remember when this long visit of Kusic took place?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: It's possible it was the end of June 1992 or the beginning of July. As for the exact date, I cannot remember, because -- actually, we could not remember dates. There weren't any calendars there or there was no other possibility of orienting oneself in terms of what day it was, what month it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. I was just asking approximately. No worries. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Approximately end of June or beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Can I now have 65 ter 28449 on the screens. And, Your Honours, maybe I can give some information about this document, because this was created by -- with the witness in preparation of his testimony on the basis of the names recognised by the witness in one of the associated exhibit, 08685, exhibit which is discussed at paragraph 82 of the witness statement. The problem we had with this exhibit, which was tendered with the witness in the Krajisnik case, is that the names identified by the witness were not visible or clear any more because they were identified through a highlighting rather than any other markings. Therefore, we have asked the witness to identify those names again, and we have put these names in a table which is now 65 ter 28449. So, first of all, I would request leave to add this to the Prosecution's 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to add this document to the 65 ter list. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, in your previous testimony in Krajisnik, you were presented with the document of the Bosnia commission for missing persons identifying the remains of victims exhumed from the Paklenik pit among others. Out of this list you identified a number of people who were from Rogatica. Now, can you please look at the names at the document on the screen. Can you tell us whether you recognise the names in the table?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And are these the names of the people from Rogatica who were hiding in cellars with you, discussed at paragraph 82 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. These are the names of people who were hiding in basements from the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to ask to clarify that for us. What you do you mean by "basement" or "cellars," and where was this and when did this episode or event happen, because that is not clear enough from your statement.

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: When I mentioned basements or cellars, I mean cellars in the centre of town, the centre of Rogatica where there are about five or six smaller and taller residential buildings, and these buildings had these cellars that many residential buildings should have, and then we hid in these cellars during the shelling of town. And sometimes we'd stay there for days. Actually, for as long as the shelling went on.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Therefore, insofar as the time-frame is concerned, I take it that these happened before people were brought to the Vlahovic Secondary School and you, yourself; right?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes. It was the time from the 21st of May up until the 6th of June when I had to go to the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you tell us if you ever saw any of these men alive after the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to them or to some of them?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: I can say -- well, actually, there were some assumptions as to what could have happened to some of the people we saw during those days, and then all of a sudden we would not see them any more. There were different assumptions, but when I arrived in the school, then we found out from one of the survivors who was in this group. He actually told us what had happened to all of these people during one of the operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you tell us what it is -- what it is that he told you happened to these people during one of the operations, one of the survivors who was in that group?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Actually, as this square is actually a rectangle, they were in a building in one of the corners, and then again this is close to the Tehnotrans company, and that's where a sniper nest was. On one occasion when the Serbian Army was shelling the area, they probably carried out this operation. I did not see that. I was in the cellar. But this witness told me about that. He said that they arrested them, tied them up with wire and took them out of Rogatica along the road towards Sarajevo, towards the greenhouse there. They took them somewhere. And at one point in time one of these Serb soldiers recognised the survivor and somehow managed to have him spared, but he had to report to the police and the guards at the secondary school centre, and that is indeed what he did, but he didn't know what happened to those other persons. He didn't know then. Later on, I and all the rest, we knew these Serb soldiers very well. We also knew the Serb police very well. And then little by little we found out from these policemen and from these Serb soldiers -- well, they basically told us all the things that had happened to them and where this group had been killed, and we then realised that all of these people who had been arrested then were killed too. That's what the Serb soldiers said. They were killed underneath the bridge in the area close to the Partisan cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this exhibit 65 ter 28449 into evidence as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28449 becomes Exhibit P314, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I now have 65 ter 12229 on the screens, please. Public display is okay for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, can you just have a look at the first page of this B/C/S document and tell me whether you recognise this document and you have reviewed it in preparation for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: This is the exhumation report from the Paklenik pit where the remains of the people from Rogatica named by the witness were identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, just a question: Do you remember identifying also in this report the names of the men from Rogatica that you knew, these men that we just saw on the table and they were hiding with you in the cellars, in the basements during the shelling of Rogatica? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will be tendering, of course, this exhumation record through proof of that witnesses, and at this time I just wanted to establish the connection between the people from Rogatica and the other evidence of the witness today. We will, of course, make the appropriate submissions as to names, et cetera, unless the Court feels that I should go through the names one by one at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber does not insist on going one by one. However, it should be clear what has been shown to the witness. 65 ter numbers are still changeable. MFI numbers are not. Madam Registrar, this document to be MFI'd and then later tendered would receive what number?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 12229 becomes Exhibit P315 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keeps that status until the Prosecution will tender it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can we now go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, my last set of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: In the meantime, could I have on the screens P178, which is the municipalities map book, and could you please turn to page 28.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement you say the two mosques of Rogatica, the Carsija mosque and the Arnaudija mosque were destroyed by the end of 1992 and only remains were left of these mosques. For the record, this is paragraph 83. You also say that you remember that one mosque was destroyed at the end of June or beginning of July and you describe how that happened. Now, do you remember which one of the two mosques was the one that was destroyed at the end of June or beginning of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: That was the upper mosque or as people used to call it, Arnaudija.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So you discussed how a soldier, Danko Neric - now, this is in the following paragraphs - was involved in the destruction of this mosque. Do you remember if he was wearing a uniform and if yes which type of uniform he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: He had an army uniform, the uniform of the former Yugoslav People's Army, colour olive drab. He didn't have a cap, but he had the insignia, because Serb soldiers habitually before any actions put insignia on their uniforms, and those were of different colours. And he had his small arms or sidearms with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, was there also a Catholic church or different Catholic churches in Rogatica, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes, opposite the Veljko Vlahovic secondary centre. That's where the Catholic church was, and that was the only Catholic church in town.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And do you know if that was destroyed, too, in the summer 1992?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: No. It remained intact, for at least as long as I was in Rogatica. I don't know what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, if you can now look at the map on the screen, this map labels the mosque in Rogatica as well as the Vlahovic Secondary School. So, now, first of all, based on your memory, do you think the -- the map or where the arrows are accurately reflects the position more or less of the -- of the mosques according to what you remember?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes. This is where they were as indicated in the map. I think it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And also if you look at the photos, for example -- and also the aerial photo of the Vlahovic school, do you think, according to what you remember, is it -- are these photos an accurate depiction of the mosque before and after the destruction and also of the aerial place where the Vlahovic school was located?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: Yes, these are accurate photographs depicting Veljko Vlahovic Secondary School and its location, and the other two photographs show the places where the mosques of Rogatica used to stand.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And now, sir, who controlled Rogatica, as far as you know, between June and December 1992?

utterances.speaker: RM081
utterances.text: During this whole period, it was the Serb army and the Serb police who had control over Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. I don't have other questions for you at this stage. Your Honours, that concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. D'Ascoli. Yes. Judge Moloto would like to ask one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one question before we leave this page here, sir. At page 73 of today's transcript, lines 4 to 8, the Prosecutor asked you this question -- well, beg your pardon, you answered the question as to what this policeman was wearing, and you said: "He had an army uniform, the uniform of the former Yugoslav People's Army, colour olive drab. He didn't have a cap," or it's written "camp" here but I heard you say cap, "but he had the insignia, because Serb soldiers habitually before any actions put insignia on their uniforms." My question to you is: What insignia did he have on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember the order of colours because that was often changed, but at that moment or on that day, I think it was red and white ribbon tied to epaulette and they were flying a bit. I remember that specifically, because I was wondering what was that, but later on through experience we learned that that was some kind of recognition sign among members of the Serb army. In the course of operation what they actually indicated and what was the meaning of those insignia I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, are you ready to start your cross-examination? Could you give us an indication as to how much type you would approximately need.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour, and I estimate approximately two hours, maybe just over two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps it's good to already inform the witness. Witness RM081, today we have another 15 minutes to go. We do not sit in this afternoon. Which means that we'll continue after the weekend, on Monday morning, but Mr. Ivetic now already starts questioning you. Mr. Ivetic, you'll find him to your left, he's standing, and Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, Witness RM081. Today I'll be asking you some questions to better understand your testimony. I propose to begin with some matters that arise out of some prior statements that were disclosed to us. To protect your identity, I therefore propose that we go into private session for these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the curtains be taken up again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: Then I'd forgotten to decide on the admission of P306 where I asked about the authorship of that document. It's already a day or two days ago. P306 is admitted into evidence. We adjourn for the day --

utterances.text: If I could, while we're finalising some of the business of the week. Mr. Vanderpuye sent me a note and he's asking that he neglected to tender 28451, so if Mr. Petrusic is able to address that just by the number, I don't have it on my screen, but I don't know if he has an objection to it, but we would tender that.
